brief.ask: Set the art direction for SIX children's picture-book templates (ids story-space, story-forest, story-ocean, story-bedtime, story-city, story-folktale; you may rename or reassign subjects if a stronger set of six emerges, but keep six). For EACH: the art-direction family and its signature (shape language, how characters/creatures are built from shapes, textures and patterns), a 6 to 8 colour palette with exact hex values that is SATURATED and high-contrast where the age band wants it, the type system (display lettering treatment, body face and size, where text sits relative to the art), the cover composition, and a spread-by-spread rhythm for the standard page set (cover, story spreads in at least five different layout types, a quiet page-turn spread, an activity page, back cover). Then decide what makes all six UNMISTAKABLY DIFFERENT from each other, and what small set of shared rules (grid, gutter, safe zones, page-turn pacing) keeps them one family. Disagree openly where you disagree.
brief.audience: Children 3 to 8 looking over a parent's shoulder or holding a tablet, and the parents/authors choosing a template for their own picture book.
brief.feeling: Joy, curiosity and a want-to-touch-it energy; a bookshop table, not a brand guideline.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Tela publication templates (services/tela/designs/publications/books.ts), children's picture books read on tablets and phones and printed (via print-on-demand) at 1024x768 landscape spreads.

Why this is being redone: the first pass (six templates: space, forest, ocean, bedtime, city, folktale) was judged by the owner as too muted, too similar to each other, tidy and adult-looking: "designed like adults are reading it to converse". They must look INVITING and EYE-CATCHING TO CHILDREN, like real art-driven picture books, and each of the six must be unmistakably different at a glance.

Research findings to design from: (1) the SPREAD is the unit, not the page; compose each two-page spread as one visual field, keep key faces/action off the gutter, let skies and grounds cross it. (2) 32-page structure: half-title, front matter, ~12-14 story spreads, back matter; the first and last pages are single pages. (3) PAGE TURNS are designed: a spread sets up the next reveal, so vary the rhythm (quiet / loud, close / wide, full-bleed / vignette / spot / sequence of small panels / colour-block pause). (4) Layout VARIETY across spreads is what makes a book feel alive: alternate full-bleed scenes, framed vignettes, spot images floating on colour, multi-panel strips, text-over-art. (5) Text is short (15 to 30 words a page), big, loosely leaded, and often HAND-LETTERED or shaped to the art, sitting INSIDE the illustration (on a banner, a cloud, a wave, a path) rather than in a neat box on top; display type acts as a character in the story. (6) Colour: bold, saturated, high-contrast for the youngest (infant studies show vivid contrast and simple big shapes hold attention best); pastels only as a deliberate choice for a calm bedtime book. (7) Ornamental flourishes and playful details add excitement. (8) The cover is a poster: one big character or shape, huge title lettering, a bright ground.

Build method (fixed): templates are drawn by deterministic TypeScript designers into Tela vector objects (rect, ellipse, path, text, images). There is no photo or illustrator input: art is procedural vector shapes (blobs, cut-paper shapes, patterns, hand-drawn-feeling paths, stylised characters built from shapes) plus labelled IMAGE SLOTS where generated art can replace it later. Decide, per template, what the procedural art actually is so the page already looks finished and joyful WITHOUT a photo.
Production of final art is GENERATIVE ONLY (no budget for commissions); procedural vector illustration must carry the templates today.

Do NOT imitate any living illustrator or copy any specific book. Name art-direction FAMILIES (cut-paper collage, mid-century geometric, wet-watercolour wash, folk/block-print, chunky crayon doodle, flat-shape minimalism, hand-inked cartoon, painted gouache night) and make Plajah-original work in them. No copyrighted characters.
Age band: 3 to 8. Must read at a glance on a phone and in print.
references: The owner's verdict on the first pass: too muted, too similar, not children's-book-looking, boring, adult.
What good looks like: art-forward spreads where the picture is the hero, text living inside the art, bold shape-driven characters, big hand-lettered titles, surprising layout changes every spread.

proposals.title: The Cantus Firmus of the Spread
proposals.idea: Six distinct physical universes bound to a singular, non-negotiable geometric proportion matrix where every saturated shape and hand-lettered line is an act of structural counterpoint.
proposals.geometry: A root-two dynamic symmetry grid applied across the 1024x768 landscape spread, establishing three primary structural axes—the horizontal center and the two golden verticals at 0.382 and 0.618—which govern safe zones, gutter protection, and the exact structural shelves where text must rest across all six layouts.
proposals.typography: Display: 'Lilita One' for geometric mass, 'DM Serif Display' for classical weight, and 'Dela Gothic One' for architectural presence. Body: 'Plus Jakarta Sans' at 18pt/24pt leaded, always tracking perfectly to the grid's horizontal subdivisions, never floating arbitrarily.
proposals.imageLogic: Six distinct procedural vector systems acting as structural armatures: 'story-space' uses hard mid-century circles and arcs in Prussian blue (#1D2A44) and cadmium orange (#FF6B35); 'story-forest' employs symmetrical woodblock silhouettes in deep pine (#1A3A2B) and vermilion (#E63946); 'story-ocean' operates on thick crayon paths of ultramarine (#0A2540) and lemon (#FFD166); 'story-bedtime' scales deep gouache night planes in indigo (#240046) and soft cream (#FFF3B0); 'story-city' builds modular architectural blocks in cadmium red (#D90429) and ochre (#F77F00); 'story-folktale' layers hard-edged cut-paper vectors in crimson (#9B2226) and sage (#52796F).
proposals.texture: Every vector surface is mapped with procedural physical noise: heavy paper tooth for the collage, endgrain wood slivers for the folktale, heavy wax-resist buildup for the ocean, and wet-pigment edge pooling for the night sky.
proposals.motion: The page-turn operates as a temporal sequence: background planes arrive at 0.6s, foreground structural shapes at 120ms depth-order, and the text settles onto its geometric shelf at 1.4s, ensuring the eye is led through a deliberate spatial descent rather than a sudden decorative reveal.
proposals.productionMethod: Deterministic TypeScript canvas builders draw the structural vector paths directly into Tela objects, while generative image slots are populated with high-fidelity, polar-coordinate shaded textures (35-degree light source) matching the scale of the child's screen.
proposals.humanTrace: The visible imperfection of physical tools: the variable ink-squeeze at the edge of the woodblock print, the physical paper-cut shadow depth, and the hand-pressed crayon drag.
proposals.risk: It risks being perceived as too rigid by those who confuse chaos with play; however, children crave structural legibility and spatial order to navigate complex, saturated visual worlds without cognitive fatigue.

arguesWith.why: The Rebellious Hand believes a mark is most expressive when it breaks the frame and rejects the grid; I contend that a mark without structural counterpoint is merely noise with confidence, and that true freedom of play requires an unyielding architecture to bounce against.

proposals.title: Unsanitized Ink and Ripped Margins
proposals.idea: Smash the sterile vector container with six aggressive, highly tactile physical methods—stencils, woodblock, heavy wax, wet bleed, torn cardboard, and raw ink-resist—using saturated, high-contrast colors that grab a child's eye with physical urgency.
proposals.geometry: A 12-field grid where the gutter is physically blocked out like masking tape on a screen-printing frame. In 'story-city', we use heavy vertical slices (stenciled spray-paint overlaps); 'story-space' forces circular planetary cutouts bleeding off-edge; 'story-ocean' runs on wave-carved horizontal splits; 'story-forest' uses thick, jagged triangular negative space; 'story-bedtime' uses slow, heavy-wax circles; 'story-folktale' runs on a rigid, off-register woodblock frame. Safe zones are treated as danger zones—characters must spill over them.
proposals.typography: Ditch the polite. We warp SVG display paths directly. 'story-space': 'Rubik Mono One' distorted to orbital paths. 'story-forest': 'Slackey' modified to look like chipped wood. 'story-ocean': 'Lakki Reddy' bleeding into the surf. 'story-bedtime': 'DynaPuff' scaled massive but softened. 'story-city': 'Bungee Outline' layered over solid 'Bungee'. 'story-folktale': 'Rubik Dirt' with deliberate off-register shadows. Body text is chunky, readable 'Fredoka' or 'Andika' (24pt to 32pt) locked inside rough-cut paper vector banners, never floating in blank space.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative assets are forced through hard threshold masks, dither matrices, and high-pressure ink-bleed shaders. No clean gradients. If we generate a space creature, it gets smashed into a 3-bit paper-cut stencil mask. 'story-ocean' uses generative wet watercolor washes masked by hard vector resist-lines. 'story-city' layers generative photographic graffiti textures over flat, screen-printed character vectors. The procedural code acts as a physical stencil frame; the generative run is the ink squeezed through it.
proposals.texture: Heavy, toothy, and non-looping. We use a custom shader that eats away at the edges of vector paths based on simulated paper-tooth noise. If a shape is large, its boundary is rough and fibrous, mimicking torn cardboard ('story-forest') or wet ink-bleed ('story-ocean'). 'story-bedtime' has the thick, greasy drag of oil pastels with visible stroke overlaps. 'story-folktale' has the dry roller-starvation of a woodblock press. Color palettes are brutally saturated: 'story-space' (#0D0015, #FF0055, #00FFCC, #FFF200, #7000FF, #FFFFFF), 'story-forest' (#0B3C1A, #FF4500, #FFD700, #8B4513, #ADFF2F, #00FF7F), 'story-ocean' (#002244, #00A8E8, #00C9A7, #FF3366, #FF9F1C, #F4F4F9), 'story-bedtime' (#120A2C, #3F2B96, #A8C0FF, #FBC707, #FF8008, #E3D2FF), 'story-city' (#1A1A1D, #C3073F, #950740, #6F2232, #4E4E50, #00FF66), 'story-folktale' (#4A1525, #C0392B, #E67E22, #F1C40F, #2C3E50, #ECF0F1).
proposals.motion: A page turn is not a slide; it is a physical flip that reveals the 'underside' of the page—a flash of raw cardboard texture or ink-smeared backing paper. Shaders drive a non-looping, low-frequency (0.6Hz) jitter on the edges of the hand-drawn-style vector paths, mimicking the micro-movements of a hand-held camera or a shaky stencil alignment. When elements transition, they snap with the suddenness of a screen-press arm coming down.
proposals.productionMethod: Procedural TypeScript vectors draw raw, jagged, non-bezier paths using chaotic midpoint displacement directly into Tela SVG layers. These vectors act as clipping paths for generative, highly saturated color-fields. A global WebGL shader reads the composite canvas, applies a 35-degree directional ink-drag (acting as our physical registration anchor), and injects a high-contrast dither matrix to ensure the colors pop with screen-printed intensity on both mobile displays and cheap POD paper.
proposals.humanTrace: The visible registration error, the bleed where two intense inks run together on the page-gutter, the frayed edge of a torn-paper vector path, and the dry-brush drag of a virtual crayon that leaves white paper-tooth gaps in the middle of a bold character's face.
proposals.risk: This risks looking messy and chaotic to conservative eyes, but it is a risk that wins because children want to see the physical struggle of mark-making. It risks looking rough when scaled down, but the high-contrast dither ensures it survives being photocopied four times on a broken office copier.

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind wants elegant proportions, harmonious type, and quiet white space. I want to smash the type into the illustration, rip the margins, and let saturated inks run wild over the gutter. Some things shouldn't resolve; they should scream.

proposals.title: The Parametric Playground
proposals.idea: Reconceptualize the children's picture book from a static gallery of nostalgic, simulated-analog surfaces into a responsive, highly saturated instrument governed by procedural vector systems and physical light axioms.
proposals.geometry: A landscape viewport (1024x768) operating on a strict three-depth-plane parallax coordinate system with a 12-column responsive grid. A 24px gutter serves as a physical collision boundary: background vectors bleed across, but active character coordinate boundaries are mathematically restricted from entering the center 48px to prevent page-fold clipping. Each of the six templates uses a distinct mathematical layout constraint: 1. story-space (Polar coordinate grid, concentric rings); 2. story-forest (Iterative branching L-systems with 45/60 degree constraint angles); 3. story-ocean (Multi-layered horizontal sine-wave bands with variable phase-shifting); 4. story-bedtime (Isometric 30-degree projection with cast shadow vectors); 5. story-city (Orthogonal grid-aligned voxels scaling dynamically based on screen-edge proximity); 6. story-folktale (Mirror-symmetric bilateral axes with radial te
proposals.typography: We reject simulated hand-lettering. We use highly legible, structurally expressive open-source typefaces scaled procedurally. 1. story-space: 'Orbitron' (Display, 48pt, uppercase, tracking 0.1) / 'Space Grotesk' (Body, 18pt, leading 1.4); 2. story-forest: 'Syne' (Display, 52pt, fluid geometric) / 'Outfit' (Body, 16pt, clean geometric); 3. story-ocean: 'Fredoka' (Display, 60pt, rounded, playful) / 'Quicksand' (Body, 18pt, soft rounded); 4. story-bedtime: 'DynaPuff' (Display, 48pt, cloud-like weight) / 'Nunito' (Body, 16pt, warm humanist); 5. story-city: 'Rubik Mono One' (Display, 44pt, architectural block) / 'Rubik' (Body, 16pt, low-contrast sans); 6. story-folktale: 'Almendra' (Display, 50pt, sharp glyphic) / 'EB Garamond' (Body, 18pt, historical structural). Text is programmatically anchored inside dynamic vector shapes (clouds, paths, buildings) to ensure it lives within the art field.
proposals.imageLogic: Image slots are not passive rectangular containers. When a generative asset is loaded, it is processed via an inline SVG filter pipeline. The system reads the image's luma channel to drive vector displacement maps, extruding 2D paths or remapping colors directly into the template's strict palette, transforming flat generative output into a physically integrated layer of the vector scene.
proposals.texture: No scanned paper textures or fake watercolor washes. Texture is defined as responsive light. A declared light source at 35°/22° serves as the generative axiom. A custom fragment shader calculates real-time vector noise, interactive foil-shimmer vectors, and micro-shadow offsets on depth-plane intersections. This makes the saturated vector blocks feel physically dimensional, solid, and tactilely responsive.
proposals.motion: On digital screens, the page-turn is an initialization routine, not a flat slide. Elements on the three depth planes arrive via a spring-mass-damper system with differentiated parallax ratios (Foreground: 1.3, Midground: 1.0, Background: 0.6). Interactive spreads respond to device tilt: a gyroscopic sensor input continuously alters the 35°/22° light vector, causing foil highlights and shadows to shift dynamically across the page.
proposals.productionMethod: Deterministic TypeScript layout designers draw raw SVG/Tela nodes. Characters are constructed on-the-fly from basic primitives (ellipses, paths, rects) using a constraint solver that ensures they never overlap text boxes. Generative image slots are populated via API calls to a latent-diffusion model, using the template's exact hexadecimal palette as hard color-matrix constraints during inference.
proposals.humanTrace: The human trace exists in the kinetic behavior and physical modeling: simulated spring-tension in vector character limbs that lag behind page movement, dragging momentum, and the intentional mathematical perturbation of vector paths using Perlin noise to create a warm, hand-drawn vector organicism without copying historical styles.
proposals.risk: This approach risks being labeled as 'digital' or 'cold' by traditionalists who equate children's books with analog nostalgia. This risk is highly worth taking: children do not have nostalgia for 19th-century lithography; they respond to luminous, high-contrast, structurally coherent systems that feel alive to their touch and render with absolute clarity on modern hardware.

arguesWith.why: The Rebellious Hand fetishizes the chaotic analog accident, dirty ink splatters, and paper tears. I build precise parametric instruments. A clean mathematical system can produce honest, infinite variation and physical warmth on purpose, under the absolute control of physics-based rules. We do not need fake dirt to make a template feel human.

proposals.title: The Theater of the Page Turn
proposals.idea: We must treat the landscape spread not as a flat grid, but as a deep, layered theatrical stage where volumetric light, extreme shadow, and scale conduct the child's eye through moments of breathtaking suspense.
proposals.geometry: A strict three-tiered depth model (foreground proscenium, midground action, background sky/horizon) mapped onto a 1024x768 canvas. The gutter is never ignored; it is treated as a natural scenic fold where characters emerge from the wings, and extreme foreground silhouettes (repoussoir) frame the central action to prevent critical details from falling into the fold.
proposals.typography: High-drama, characterful open-license display faces acting as physical scenery. 'Chango' for story-space (bold, orbital curves); 'Cinzel Decorative' for story-forest (gothic, branching serifs); 'Rubik Beastly' for story-ocean (tentacled, fluid weight); 'Playfair Display Black' for story-bedtime (stately, heavy-contrast lullaby); 'Bungee' for story-city (towering, blocky verticality); and 'Almendra Display' for story-folktale (medieval, hand-carved rhythm). Body text is set in 'Fraunces' or 'Lora' (18pt to 24pt), nestled into environmental light pockets.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative vector layouts composed as flat scenic layers. Each template features one dominant, simulated light source—an orbital sun, a bioluminescent swell, a streetlamp cone, a bedside candle—that propagates its angle across all vector boundaries, casting procedural drop shadows and highlight offsets that give flat shapes an arresting, three-dimensional presence.
proposals.texture: Tactile, heavy-weight paper tooth, velvet shadow depth achieved through CSS multiply filters, and a simulated 35-degree metallic foil shader that shimmers on tablet tilt, transforming vector borders into gilded proscenium edges.
proposals.motion: The page-turn is a curtain pull. The rhythm is composed of sharp contrasts: Spread 1 (The Overture: full-bleed saturated color), Spread 2 (The Whisper: quiet spot illustration on dark ground), Spread 3 (The Crescendo: dramatic double-page landscape), Spread 4 (The Intrigue: multi-panel comic strips), Spread 5 (The Reveal: blinding light-burst), Spread 6 (The Epilogue: soft, fading focus).
proposals.productionMethod: Deterministic TypeScript rendering layered SVG paths with inline CSS radial gradients and blend modes. Rather than flat fills, procedural vector shaders simulate volumetric light beams, dust motes, and soft-focus bokeh directly inside the SVG DOM, delivering high-end depth at zero asset cost.
proposals.humanTrace: Varied vector stroke weights that mimic the physical pressure of a wet ink brush, soft watercolor bleeding along the edges of the vector shadows, and simulated lens flare artifacts that suggest a human eye is staging the scene.
proposals.risk: The sheer scale of the visual drama risks overwhelming the short text blocks, but this is a risk worth taking because children do not fall in love with neat margins—they fall in love with worlds they can get lost inside.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist's insistence on flat, empty spaces is a desert for a child's imagination. Restraint is not a virtue when you have a stage to fill; it is an alibi for not deciding what the world should feel like.

proposals.title: The Architecture of Primary Joy
proposals.idea: We rescue these templates from adult tidiness not by adding decorative noise, but by reducing each book to one absolute geometric constraint and one unyielding color contrast that children can read from across a room.
proposals.geometry: A strict 1024x768 landscape grid split by a single, unyielding mathematical axis. Each of the six books is governed by a singular, non-negotiable shape language: 'space' uses only perfect circles (planets, orbits); 'forest' uses only vertical columns (trunks, light beams); 'ocean' uses only horizontal bands (tides, horizons); 'bedtime' uses only nesting concentric arcs (lunar phases, blankets); 'city' uses only 90-degree orthogonal blocks (towers, windows); and 'folktale' uses only 45-degree diagonal triangles (tangrams, peaks). No freehand curves are permitted.
proposals.typography: We banish polite, small-scale body copy. We use only two open-licensed geometric powerhouses: 'League Spartan' for monumental, single-word displays integrated directly into the layout's primary shapes, and 'Rubik' for body text, set at a minimum of 24pt with 1.5 line height, sitting in dedicated, high-contrast structural negative spaces rather than floating aimlessly over illustrations.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative SVGs constructed entirely through boolean path operations. There are no illustrated character details or facial features—character presence is established purely through scale, color contrast, and orientation of the primary shapes (e.g., a massive red circle represents the giant; a tiny yellow circle represents the child). No gradients or complex textures are generated; colors are flat, hard-edged vector volumes.
proposals.texture: The zero-fuzz digital edge. We reject simulated paper tooth and watercolor washes as sentimental. The texture is the absolute, unyielding density of solid color blocks—specifically, simulated silk-screen ink density where overlay areas create a third, mathematically calculated color lane (e.g., yellow over blue creates a sharp, untextured green strip at the intersection).
proposals.motion: Zero decorative eases or spring physics. Transitions on digital devices are immediate, hard-cut state changes or linear page-turns that operate precisely along the layout's primary geometric axis, treating the screen transition as a physical shutter.
proposals.productionMethod: A deterministic TypeScript layout generator that restricts the canvas to a maximum of seven vector paths per spread. The engine calculates layout variety not by introducing new elements, but by programmatically scaling, shifting, and color-inverting the existing shape-hierarchy on every page turn.
proposals.humanTrace: The tension of the boundary line. The human hand is felt in the radical, deliberate editing of the composition—the exact, millimeter-precise placement of the negative space that forces the eye to complete the unfinished shape.
proposals.risk: This direction risks looking too stark to parents who equate children's literature with soft, illustrative clutter; it is worth it because children possess an innate, highly developed sensitivity to pure form, scale, and high-contrast composition that busy layouts only disrupt.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist wants to pile on details, lighting effects, and narrative clutter to 'create a world.' I want to give the child three massive, primary-colored shapes and the silence of a blank page, allowing their own imagination to perform the heavy lifting.
